title: Multiplication Facts and Multiplying 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Multiplication – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Recall multiplication facts up to 9 × 9; multiply 2-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers; multiply three 1-digit numbers; use the property of zero and one. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on multiplication: times tables up to 9 × 9, multiplying 2-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers, multiplying by 0 and 1, and multiplying three numbers. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
  • To multiply 23 × 4, multiply the units and the tens: 3 × 4 = 12 and 20 × 4 = 80, so 23 × 4 = 92.
  • Any number × 0 = 0. Any number × 1 = the same number. 3 × 5 = 5 × 3.

Examples

Example

36 × 3

6 × 3 = 18, write 8 carry 1

3 × 3 + 1 = 10

Answer: 108

Example

4 × 2 × 5

4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 5

Answer: 40

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of multiplying3 × 4 = 12, not 7.
Forgetting to carryAdd the carried number after multiplying the tens.
Thinking 7 × 0 = 7Zero groups of anything is 0.

items.q: The red hand is the minute hand. How many minutes past 3 is it?
items.e: The minute hand points to 4. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So it is 20 minutes past 3.

items.q: The red hand is the minute hand. How many minutes past 2 is it?
items.e: The minute hand points to 9. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. So it is 45 minutes past 2.

items.e: Partition 78 into 70 + 8. Multiply both parts by 5, then add: 70 × 5 + 8 × 5 = 350 + 40 = 390.

items.q: What is 40 × 3? Think: 4 × 3 = 12.
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. 4 tens × 3 = 12 tens = 120. 12 tens = 1 hundred and 2 tens.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 27 × 8 = 20 × 8 + ☐ × 8
items.e: 27 = 20 + 7, so 27 × 8 = 20 × 8 + 7 × 8. The missing number is 7.

items.q: What is 20 × 4? Think: 2 × 4 = 8.
items.e: 20 is 2 tens. 2 tens × 4 = 8 tens = 80. Not 8: that would be ones, not tens.

items.q: Use the grid method to find 18 × 5.
Use short multiplication.
items.e: Units: 4 × 8 = 32. Write 2, exchange 3 tens. Tens: 9 × 8 + 3 = 75. Write 75. Answer: 752.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Units: 3 × 4 = 12. Write 2, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 7 × 4 + 1 = 29. Write 29. Answer: 292.

items.q: What is 13 × 3?
items.e: Units: 3 × 3 = 9. Tens: 1 × 3 = 3. Multiply both digits. Answer: 39.

items.q: What is 12 × 2?
items.e: Units: 2 × 2 = 4. Tens: 1 × 2 = 2. Multiply both digits. Answer: 24.

items.q: The ones are done. Now the tens: 8 × 4, then add the exchanged 1. What is the full answer?
items.e: Multiply first, then add: 8 × 4 + 1 = 33. The tens are the last column, so write all of 33. Answer: 336.

items.q: What is 42 × 8?
items.e: Units: 2 × 8 = 16. Write 6, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 4 × 8 + 1 = 33. Write 33. Answer: 336.

items.q: Start with the units: 7 × 4 = 28. What do you do?
items.e: 28 units = 2 tens and 8 units. Write 8 in the units column. Exchange 2 tens: write a small 2 under the tens column. Units: 7 × 4 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 8 × 4 + 2 = 34. Write 34. Answer: 348.

items.q: What is 57 × 5?
items.e: Units: 7 × 5 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3 tens. Tens: 5 × 5 + 3 = 28. Write 28. Answer: 285.

items.q: Start with the units: 3 × 5 = 15. What do you do?
items.e: 15 units = 1 ten and 5 units. Write 5 in the units column. Exchange 1 ten: write a small 1 under the tens column. Units: 3 × 5 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 2 × 5 + 1 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 115.

items.q: The ones are done. Now the tens: 6 × 8, then add the exchanged 5. What is the full answer?
items.e: Multiply first, then add: 6 × 8 + 5 = 53. The tens are the last column, so write all of 53. Answer: 536.

items.q: What is 8 × 1?
items.e: Any number times 1 is that same number. 8 × 1 = 8. (1 group of 8, or 8 groups of 1.)

items.q: What is 1 × 6?
items.e: Any number times 1 is that same number. 1 × 6 = 6. (1 group of 6, or 6 groups of 1.)

items.q: What is 10 × 1?
items.e: Any number times 1 is that same number. 10 × 1 = 10. (1 group of 10, or 10 groups of 1.)

items.q: What is 1 × 3?
items.e: Any number times 1 is that same number. 1 × 3 = 3. (1 group of 3, or 3 groups of 1.)

items.q: What is 0 × 7?
items.e: Any number times 0 is 0. 0 × 7 means 0 groups of 7, so there is nothing at all. (Writing a 0 after the number is the rule for × 10, not × 0.)

items.q: What is 9 × 0?
items.e: Any number times 0 is 0. 9 × 0 means 9 groups of 0, so there is nothing at all. (Writing a 0 after the number is the rule for × 10, not × 0.)

items.q: What is 0 × 4?
items.e: Any number times 0 is 0. 0 × 4 means 0 groups of 4, so there is nothing at all. (Writing a 0 after the number is the rule for × 10, not × 0.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? × 7 = 7
items.e: Only 1 keeps the number the same: 1 × 7 = 7. 0 × 7 is 0, and 7 × 7 is 49.

items.q: Find the missing number: 8 × ? = 0
items.e: A product is 0 only when you multiply by 0: 8 × 0 = 0. 8 × 1 is 8.

items.q: The second array is the first one turned on its side. Which equation do the two arrays show?
items.e: Turning an array does not add or remove any dots. Both have 15 dots, so 3 × 5 = 5 × 3. This is the commutative property.
